content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Edward Fleming (E042) requests write access to Source Code.

Two notes:
- Note 1 (HR): role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation write.
- Note 2 (Security): role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Comment says Security DB is authoritative and differs from prior team note listing full_time.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by Engineer role. Edward is Payroll Specialist, so not admin anyway.

The conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor with basic training. The Security note says Security DB is authoritative. So the employee is a contractor with basic security training.

For contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

Wait, but need to consider whose authority matters. Security record is authoritative for employment type? The note says "Security DB is authoritative". So contractor, basic training. Maximum = read. Requested = write. Above max, so grant max = read.

Also never grant more than requested. Write requested, so at most write. Grant read.

So decision: read.

Evidence: Security note indicates contractor with basic training; contractors without advanced training max is read; write requested exceeds max so grant read.
